diagnostic_evidence.quote: as \( N \) tends to infinity, while \( d/N \rightarrow \gamma \in (0,1) \), \( m_i/N \rightarrow \xi \in (\gamma, 1) \), the \(i\)-th relative prediction efficiency $\mathrm{PE}(i)$ has the limit \[ \mathrm{PE}(i) = \frac{\mathbb{E}\|X\tilde{\beta}^i - X\beta\|^2}{\mathbb{E}\|X\hat{\beta} - X\beta\|^2} = \frac{1 - \gamma}{\xi - \gamma}. \]

According to Lemma \ref{lemma:lemma3}, when \( \xi > m_i / N > d/N > \gamma \), it follows that \begin{align*} \text{PE}(i) & \leq \frac{1- d/N}{m_i/N - d/N} \\ & = \frac{N - d}{m_i - d}, \end{align*}
Therefore, the subsequent discussions are based on the following conditions:

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem Thf and Lemma finalerror are stated as finite-N guarantees holding with probability at least 1-2δ, but their proofs' per-subproblem precision floor E||X(β̃^i-β)|| ≤ √((N-d)/(m_i-d))·E||X(β̂-β)|| is justified only by Lemma lemma:lemma3, which is an asymptotic limit (N→∞ with d/N→γ and m_i/N→ξ). Remark remarkA7 converts that limit into a finite-N inequality by a monotonicity heuristic that treats the limit value g(γ,ξ) as the finite-N ratio and mixes the limit ξ with the finite m_i/N, and the resulting first-moment bound additionally needs a variance condition that is stated only in that remark ('the subsequent discussions are based on the following conditions') and appears in no theorem hypothesis. Hence the advertised finite-N, high-probability, OLS-level precision guarantee is unsupported as stated; the given argument establishes it at best in the asymptotic regime with extra conditions.

failure_location.quote: with probability at least \(1-2\delta\), for any \(\beta_0 \in \mathbb{R}^{d}\), it holds that \begin{align}\label{final_precision} \mathbb{E}\|X(\beta_T- {\beta})\| \leq (\frac{1}{3} )^{T} \mathbb{E}\|X(\beta_{0}-\beta )\| + [1+o(1)]\mathbb{E}\|X(\hat{\beta}-\beta )|,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either (i) restate Lemma finalerror and Theorem Thf as asymptotic results (N→∞ with d/N→γ, m_i/N→ξ_i) and add the variance condition of Remark remarkA7 as an explicit hypothesis — withdrawing the advertised finite-N, high-probability guarantee — or (ii) establish finite-N versions of E||X(β̃^i-β)|| ≤ √((N-d)/(m_i-d))·E||X(β̂-β)|| under the theorems' stated hypotheses, which the source does not provide.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central convergence guarantee — Theorem Thf: with probability ≥ 1-2δ, SLSE-FRS attains the OLS (noise-level) precision [1+o(1)]E||X(β̂-β)|| at rate 1/3 — is not established for finite N. The gap propagates through Lemma finalerror (whose per-subproblem floor √((N-d)/(m_i-d))·E||X(β̂-β)|| drives the whole induction), Theorem lowerBoundai (whose error-ratio inequality rests on the same asymptotic PE bound), and Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE (whose iteration-count bounds inherit it). The abstract/introduction promise that SLSE-FRS 'achieves the same level of precision as the OLS estimator' is supported only asymptotically.
issues.title: OLS-level precision guarantee of SLSE-FRS rests on an asymptotic PE bound applied as a finite-N inequality, with an unstated variance condition
issues.why_classification: Serious: the advertised finite-N, high-probability OLS-precision guarantee cannot be established from the source's arguments; every supported resolution either excludes the advertised finite-N regime (the guarantee type changes to an asymptotic one) or requires new finite-N proof architecture. No comparable finite-N version of the main claim survives, and the paper's central promise depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Theorem \ref{lowerBoundai} implies that the sequence $\{a_i\}_{i=2}^K$ are monotonically increasing with respect to $i$, namely \(a_2<\ldots<a_K\)

issues.failure_explanation: The statement defines r(i-1,i) = √((m_{i-1}-d)/(m_i-d)) (the flattened radical reads as this fraction), which is < 1 because the sketch sizes increase. But the bound is derived by requiring r to dominate the error ratio E||X(β̃^{i-1}-β)||/E||X(β̃^i-β)||, which is > 1 (a smaller sketch gives a worse estimator); the proof correctly uses r(i-1,i) = √((m_i-d)/(m_{i-1}-d)) > 1. Thus the statement's r is the reciprocal of the proof's r: the stated lower bound is weaker than the bound the proof establishes, and if it is used as the actual iteration count — as Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE does ('let a_i take exactly their lower bounds') — the contraction estimate no longer guarantees the stopping criterion (14). With the correct r, a_i = log_3([1+(1+ω)√((m_i-d)/(m_{i-1}-d))]/ω) is decreasing in i (since √((2u-1)/(u-1)) decreases in u = m_{i-1}/d), so the claimed monotonicity a_2<...<a_K is reversed, the bound a_i < α = log_3([1+(1+ω)/√2]/ω) fails (the maximum is a_2 = log_3([1+(1+ω)√((2^{-K+1}-γ)/(2^{-K}-γ))]/ω), which diverges as γ→2^{-K}), and the 1st-stage cost '4αNd' is understated.

failure_location.quote: a_i \geq \log_3 \left[ \frac{(1+\omega)r(i-1, i) + 1}{\omega} \right] > 0, \] where \( r(i-1,i) = \sqrt{m_{i-1} - d / m_{i} - d} \).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the fraction in Theorem lowerBoundai's statement to r(i-1,i) = √((m_i-d)/(m_{i-1}-d)) (matching its proof), then re-derive Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE: with the corrected r the sequence a_i is decreasing in i, its maximum is a_2 = log_3([1+(1+ω)√((2^{-K+1}-γ)/(2^{-K}-γ))]/ω), and the 1st-stage dominant cost becomes 4a_2Nd; the initialization-dominated and O(Nd) asymptotic conclusions survive with the corrected constant.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE's quantitative claims are false as stated: the iteration counts are claimed to increase with i (in fact they decrease under the correct r), the explicit bound a_i < α = log_3([1+(1+ω)/√2]/ω) fails (a_2 can be much larger and diverges as γ→2^{-K}), and the 1st-stage dominant cost '4αNd' is understated (correct: 4a_2Nd with a_2 = log_3([1+(1+ω)√((2^{-K+1}-γ)/(2^{-K}-γ))]/ω)). The Section-3 prose claim that {a_i}_{i=2}^K is monotonically increasing, and the experimental guidance built on it, inherit the error. The asymptotic conclusions that initialization (Ndlog_2N) dominates and that total cost is O(Nd) when log_2N=O(1) survive with corrected constants.
issues.title: r(i-1,i) in the lowerBoundai statement is the reciprocal of the error-ratio bound used in its proof, corrupting the complexity theorem's quantitative claims
issues.why_classification: Moderate: the root is an inversion in the r definition (the statement's fraction is the reciprocal of the proof's), and the repair is that correction plus a contained re-derivation of the complexity theorem's bounds; no new proof architecture is needed and the asymptotic complexity conclusions survive, but the stated monotonicity direction, the explicit constant α, and the 1st-stage cost necessarily change, so it is more than a local typo fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma's proof contracts the bipartite state (β_t-β̂, β_{t-1}-β̂) by the iteration matrix L; after t-T† steps the resulting bound involves the norm of the whole initial pair (X(β_{T†}-β̂), X(β_{T†-1}-β̂)). The 1st-stage proof could reduce to a single initial error only because it imposed the equal pair β_{-1}^i = β_0^i. The 2nd stage of Algorithm Alg-SRHT starts the loop at t = T† with the pair inherited from the 1st stage, whose two components are not equal, so the proof cannot discard ||X(β_{T†-1}-β̂)||; the claimed bound ||X(β_t-β̂)|| ≤ (1/3)^{t-T†}||X(β_{T†}-β̂)|| does not follow (the displayed intermediate '(1/3)^t' should in any case read '(1/3)^{t-T†}'). Theorem Thf's proof applies this lemma, so its transient term (1/3)^T·E||X(β_0-β)|| is unsupported as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert a one-line equal-pair initialization at the start of the 2nd stage of Algorithm Alg-SRHT (set β_{T†-1} ← β_{T†} before the loop), which makes the lemma's proof valid exactly as written via the same √2/Gelfand argument as in Theorem thm:convergence_theorem1; alternatively, repair the lemma to bound both initial errors, E||X(β_T-β̂)|| ≤ (1/3)^{T-T†}[E||X(β_{T†}-β̂)|| + E||X(β_{T†-1}-β̂)||], and re-run Theorem Thf's combination, which changes the transient coefficient from (1/3)^T to 4·(1/3)^T while preserving the rate 1/3 and the OLS-precision floor.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma M-IHS converging rate's stated contraction of the 2nd stage toward β̂ is unproven as written; Theorem Thf's transient term (1/3)^T·E||X(β_0-β)|| relies on it. The rate-1/3 contraction and the [1+o(1)]·E||X(β̂-β)|| precision floor can be preserved only after either a one-line change to the algorithm's 2nd-stage initialization or a small strengthening of the lemma's bound (which changes the transient constant to 4·(1/3)^T).
issues.title: Second-stage contraction lemma (M-IHS converging rate) drops the second initial iterate's error; Theorem Thf inherits the gap
issues.why_classification: Moderate: the lemma's proof has a genuine gap (a dropped initial-error term) and the main theorem Thf depends on it, but a complete resolution is contained — either a one-line construction change to the algorithm's 2nd-stage initialization or a small new argument weakening only the transient constant — with the rate and precision-floor guarantees preserved.
